title: Cargo Manifest Upload
description: A logistics partner sends a CSV of shipments to bulk-import. Some rows are well-formed, some reference a customer that doesn't exist, and some have garbage numeric fields. Prove the import validates and reports on every row independently rather than accepting or rejecting the whole file.
successCondition: POST /api/admin/shipments/import with a CSV containing one fully valid row, one row with an unknown customerEmail, and one row with a non-numeric weightKg returns 200 with totalRows 3, accepted 1, rejected 2, and a rows array where each rejected row lists a human-readable reason. GET /api/tracking afterward shows exactly one new shipment was actually created — the rejected rows were never persisted.
hints: Required CSV columns are documented in docs/api/admin.md — the file is uploaded as multipart/form-data with a field named "file".
Origin/destination labels can legitimately contain commas (e.g. "Port of Los Angeles, CA, USA") — a correct test CSV quotes those fields.
